name: GlassPageBuilder

stories.notes: Story decorator force-overrides every button with !important background/color/border (stories.tsx:9-25), so screenshots show story CSS, not component styling. Docs blurb claims 'revolutionary', 'Full history management with keyboard shortcuts', 'Auto-save every 30s' - shortcuts are no-ops.

tests.notes: Templated smoke/axe/className/snapshot tests only; className test passes via container.firstChild fallback; nothing exercises drag/drop, undo, save, publish.

material_impl: Glass primitive only inside child panels; toolbar/status bar use glass-surface-subtle/primary utility classes; GlassPageBuilder.css adds bespoke .glass-cms-control-frost with hard-coded rgba(255,255,255,.24), blur(16px) saturate(1.5) and !important (GlassPageBuilder.css:3-15). Mixed Tailwind (bg-white/15, rounded-md, px-3) and glass-* utilities in same className strings (GlassPageBuilder.tsx:155-191). Emoji used as icons throughout.
motion: transition-colors only; useReducedMotion imported but unused (line 17). No motion system.
a11y: Icon-only undo/redo buttons rely on title only (163,175) - no aria-label; breakpoint buttons not a radiogroup/aria-pressed; Grid/Snap toggles lack aria-pressed; tablet and mobile share the same 📱 icon (54-55). h-screen root traps layout. Keyboard shortcuts preventDefault Ctrl+Z/Y/S/P globally on document but do nothing (312-342) - breaks browser save/print and undo in any input on the page.
api: Plain React.FC, no forwardRef, no style passthrough. onSave/onPreview/onPublish props are accepted but NEVER called (326-334, 247-250 uses alert('Page published! (Demo)')). initialData typed loosely and passed through as Partial<PageExportData> cast. Hard-coded localStorage key 'glass-page-builder-autosave' with auto-load on mount when no initialData (299) - multiple builders on a page collide.
ssr: 'use client'; window/localStorage accessed only in effects/handlers (OK). Imports a global CSS file from a component (line 18) - breaks Next.js pages-router consumers that disallow global CSS imports from node_modules components.
fake_complexity: High. Publish = alert. Keyboard shortcuts = commented-out no-ops. Status bar hard-codes 'Zoom: 100%' and `Grid: ${false ? 'ON':'OFF'}` (436) regardless of state. 'Auto-save: ON' static text. Snap-to-grid toggles a flag nothing reads. Version badge 'v1.0' hard-coded. Auto-save interval derived from ANIMATION.DURATION.slower*42 (=29.4s) - animation token abused as timer.
justification: A design-system library should not ship a half-built page-builder application. Its public callbacks are never invoked, Publish is an alert(), keyboard shortcuts hijack Ctrl+S/Z/P and do nothing, the status bar is static text, and the underlying provider's moveComponent is a no-op so reordering silently fails. Its rendered button styling in certification comes from a story decorator with !important overrides, so the screenshot is not evidence of component quality. Combined with the new Function() script execution in GlassCanvas, this is a liability. If a builder is strategically wanted, it belongs in a separate example app built on real primitives (Toolbar, SegmentedControl, TreeView, Inspector), not in the 5.0 core package.
visual_review: Screenshot PNGs exist (1440x900 desktop, 390x844 mobile) but the image reader returned no content in the verification pass, so visual scores rely on code review plus the automated audit (reports/audit/blocked-61.md) rather than direct visual inspection.

name: GlassCanvas

stories.notes: Single empty-state story; never shows rendered components, selection, or drop zones.

tests.notes: Templated; focus tests guarded by `if (element)` so they pass vacuously; no render-of-components test.

material_impl: Wraps Glass primitive, then overrides inner surface with inline backgroundColor 'rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.18)' (517); selection/drop states use raw Tailwind blue (bg-blue-500, ring-blue-500, border-blue-500) not tokens (69-70, 406, 535).
motion: Dynamic Tailwind arbitrary classes built with template literals `duration-[${ANIMATION.DURATION.fast}ms]` (64, 405, 525, 534) - JIT cannot see these, so the classes do not exist. useReducedMotion called but result unused (442).
a11y: role='main' on an embeddable canvas (488) - conflicts with page landmarks. Canvas items are draggable divs with onClick/onDoubleClick and no tabIndex/role/keyboard handlers - unusable by keyboard. Empty state uses emoji and tells users 'Use Ctrl+Z to undo' which the builder does not implement. Inline edit input has no label.
api: React.FC, className + data-testid only; no forwardRef/style. Depends on useDragDrop context; silently falls back to a no-op default context when used outside a provider (GlassDragDropProvider.tsx:923-926).
fake_complexity: SECURITY: button component executes arbitrary user-entered strings via `new Function(onClickScript)()` (315) with default prop 'alert("Button clicked!")' (GlassDragDropProvider.tsx:374) - stored XSS if page JSON is imported/shared (importPage accepts any JSON). Every component's full props object is spread into inline style (107-109), leaking 'content', 'text', 'onClick' into CSS. ComponentRenderer passes the parent's isSelected down to all children (140,177,213,378) so selecting a container highlights every descendant. Drop zones never set dragOverTarget, so 'before/after' active states never light up (setDragOverTarget only resets).
justification: This canvas runs code with new Function(), puts all component data into inline styles, highlights every child when one is selected, has drop zones that never activate, and builds Tailwind classes at runtime that never get generated. It cannot be used from the keyboard, and it claims role=main. Polishing would not fix it. Remove it along with the CMS suite.

Nothing here can be reused that the library doesn't already offer better (search field, accordion, list). Remove it together with the CMS suite.

name: GlassDragDropProvider (DragDropProvider)

stories.notes: Story just renders GlassCanvas inside; screenshot byte-identical to GlassCanvas story.

tests.notes: Templated; zero tests of add/move/delete/undo logic.

material_impl: Non-visual; renders wrapper div with class 'glass-dragdrop-provider'. Default library uses hard-coded via.placeholder.com image URL (339) - a third-party domain that has been unreliable.
a11y: n/a (no keyboard DnD model at all; HTML5 DnD only, no touch support).
api: forwardRef + HTMLAttributes passthrough (good). Context value object recreated every render (826-856) - every consumer re-renders on any state change. componentLibrary not configurable via props. useDragDrop returns a silent no-op default when no provider (923-926) - misuse is invisible.
fake_complexity: moveComponent is a stub: '// Implementation for moving components within the tree' then saveToHistory() (659-665) - all element reordering silently does nothing. addComponent 'inside' mutates existing state object (target.children.push, 548) - violates immutability, breaks history snapshots (history stores shallow copies sharing mutated children). deleteComponent also mutates component.children (606). Nested children are never rendered as roots but also never flagged; duplicateComponent always appends to root. updateComponent does not record history, so property edits are not undoable. onDrop closes over dragDropState but addComponent/moveComponent are declared after it and omitted from deps (494-514).
duplicates: any dnd-kit style sortable in library
justification: The page-builder state engine has a stub move operation, mutates state in place, leaves property edits out of undo, can't be configured, and has no keyboard or touch drag-and-drop. It is application code, not a design-system primitive. If 5.0 wants drag-and-drop, it should provide a headless sortable primitive (or wrap dnd-kit) with proper keyboard semantics. This file is not a starting point for that.

It has no tree semantics, its row actions only appear on hover, every component shows a 'Hidden' badge because of a logic bug, and its import path is unvalidated. Remove it with the CMS suite, and point any tree need to the single consolidated TreeView.

motion: FAB opacity transition 160ms hard-coded (1450); spinner glass-animate-spin; no reduced-motion handling (hook imported, unused, line 31).
a11y: role='main' + aria-live='polite' on the whole workspace (431-432) - every re-render text change would be announced; also nests a main landmark. api: Function component, no forwardRef. Required props userId/userName/userEmail/userRole/userAvatar are destructured away and never used (244-247). theme, enableScreenSharing, onUserJoined, onUserLeft, onError, enableSnapping, showRulers accepted and ignored. ssr: 'use client'. Wraps in CollaborationProvider which WILL open a real WebSocket if NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBSOCKET_SERVER_URL is set, while the UI ignores provider state entirely and uses a hard-coded mock context (248-326).
fake_complexity: Self-declared '@demo DEMO / SHOWCASE COMPONENT' (2-9). Entire collaboration context is a literal mock object (isConnected:true, 3 fake users, all actions () => {}). Canvas is a placeholder emoji with 'Click to start designing together' (1009-1015) and no click handler. Mini Map = text 'Canvas overview'. Voice chat, snapshots, undo/redo, copy/paste/delete all no-ops. Connection error Retry is () => {}.
justification: This is a 1,547-line mock that ships in the root bundle. Its own header comment says it is a demo. Every action is a no-op, its user props are ignored, and its fake 'connected' state disagrees with the real provider it wraps (which may open a live socket). Exporting it from the package root signals capabilities that don't exist. At most it should move to a Storybook-only showcase or a docs example. Also: the inline <style> block is injected again for every instance, and WorkspaceFloatingActions/VoiceChatPanel/VersionControlPanel use glass-fixed (1332, 1381, 1441), so they escape any contained or compact host.

name: GlassCollaborationProvider (CollaborationProvider, useCollaboration)

stories.notes: Stories render GlassCollaborationDashboard's demo fallback with enableRealTime off; screenshot text identical to Dashboard story ('ALO3 online ○Disconnected').

material_impl: Non-visual. generateUserColor picks random token colors with Math.random (158-172) - non-deterministic, SSR/hydration-unstable if used during render.
motion: n/a. Timers derived from animation tokens: heartbeat ANIMATION.DURATION.slower*25 (=17.5s, 329), reconnect cap slower*50 (=35s), cursor debounce fast/4 (=37.5ms, 394).
api: Two names for same thing (CollaborationProvider + GlassCollaborationProvider alias). maxUsers prop ignored. No way to inject a transport/adapter (Yjs, Liveblocks, custom) - URL comes only from env vars. Context value not memoized (538-559). data-glass-component passed to Context.Provider (562) is meaningless. useCollaboration silently returns a no-op default when no provider (143-146).
ssr: 'use client'. Reads process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBSOCKET_SERVER_URL / WEBSOCKET_SERVER_URL inside a published library effect (284-287): in a Vite/browser bundle with no process shim this throws ReferenceError; in Next it only works if the consumer's bundler inlines env for node_modules code. Exposing a server-only env name (WEBSOCKET_SERVER_URL) in client code is a smell.
fake_complexity: Partially real: an actual WebSocket client with backoff and heartbeat. But: no auth/token on the socket; inbound selection_update/comment_resolved/reply messages are never handled; replyToComment never sends to server (452-475); remote cursor positions are absolute viewport px with no element anchoring; current user's cursor is only broadcast if consumer calls updateCursor. Ad-hoc JSON protocol undocumented.
target: headless presence adapter interface (subscribe/publish) consumed by a single GlassPresence/GlassCursors visual layer; transport supplied by consumer
justification: This is the only file in the collaboration folder that does real work. A design system should still not own a bespoke WebSocket protocol configured through env vars. For 5.0 it should become a thin, documented adapter contract (users, cursors, comments) with a reference in-memory adapter for docs. Real transports (Liveblocks/Yjs/PartyKit or the app's own) should plug in from outside. If the team does not want to maintain an adapter, it should be removed.

name: GlassCollaborationDashboard
material_impl: Glass primitive for collapsed/expanded shells; avatars filled with raw user.color with glass-text-primary letters (no contrast check); hard-coded demo hex colors #38bdf8/#a3e635/#f59e0b.
motion: transition-colors only; no reduced-motion need, none wired.
a11y: Close button '✕' without aria-label (351-356). Tabs lack tablist/tab/aria-selected. Toggle buttons (Cursors/Comments/Activity) lack aria-pressed. Status conveyed by emoji colored dots + color classes. Collapsed trigger has no aria-expanded.
ssr: Date.now() during render for active/away status (80, 291, 450) - hydration mismatch risk and no re-render over time, so 'Away' never updates.
fake_complexity: When provider has no data it silently fabricates demo users/activities (273-280) - in production an empty room shows fake people 'Aurora/Lumen/Orbit' with example.com emails. That is a correctness bug, not a demo affordance.
target: GlassPresence (single presence/avatar-stack + activity popover built on GlassAvatarGroup + GlassPopover/Tabs)
justification: A presence pill with an activity popover is a legitimate pattern, and this widget is the most coherent visual in the collaboration folder. But it overlaps with at least three other presence components, it injects fake users in production when data is empty, it computes status with Date.now() during render, and its tabs and toggles have no ARIA. Fold its layout into one consolidated GlassPresence that uses the library's Avatar, Popover and Tabs primitives, with demo data kept in stories only.

name: GlassCollaborativeComments
material_impl: Glass primitive for bubbles; pointer triangle hard-coded rgba(255,255,255,0.9) (296, 659) which will be wrong in dark themes; resolved border rgba(148,163,184,.8). Styles applied imperatively via refs in useEffect 'without JSX style attribute' (64-94, 312-319) while the same elements also use JSX style - inconsistent and causes a first-paint jump (unpositioned until effect).
a11y: Comments can only be created by double-click on the container (413-449) - no keyboard path. Resolve button '✓' title-only. Textareas without labels. Click-outside overlay is a fixed inset div with onClick, no Escape handling. Dots labelled just 'Comment'/'Resolved comment' without author/content.
api: React.FC; className/compact/contained/maxHeight/aria-label. Positions are absolute px relative to container - no element anchoring.
ssr: DEMO_COMMENTS timestamps computed at module load with Date.now() (26, 35, 43) - stale and hydration-unstable.
fake_complexity: Falls back to demo comment when provider empty (372-376). In that demo mode currentUser is null, so provider.addComment returns early (GlassCollaborationProvider.tsx:418) - new comments silently vanish. Replies are always attributed to the parent comment's author (254 'In real app, would look up by reply.userId').

It drops comments silently in its default demo mode, credits every reply to the wrong author, and positions bubbles imperatively in a way that makes them jump. Merge the thread UI into GlassCommentThread. Pin positioning should become a small anchored-popover primitive that keyboard users can reach.

material_impl: Not glass at all: solid user.color label background with glass-text-primary text (42-44) - contrast depends on random color; SVG cursor with white stroke.

Keep one cursor component that takes container-relative coordinates, uses a glass label with contrast-safe text, and respects reduced motion. Delete the rest.

name: CookieConsent
material_impl: CSS module with tokenized aura vars: background var(--aura-color-glass-surface), border var(--aura-color-glass-border), backdrop-filter var(--glass-cookie-backdrop-filter, blur(var(--glass-blur-md,24px)) var(--glass-filter-base)) (CookieConsent.module.css:11-19). Best-tokenized surface in this shard. However --cookie-blur-scale is set from glassIntensity but never consumed by CSS, so glassIntensity only changes shadow length (176-181).
motion: useGalileoStateSpring springs for opacity/translateY with immediate when reduced-motion or disableAnimation (97-171) - reduced motion genuinely wired. But hidden state returns display:none immediately (189-199), so exit animation never plays; CSS transition on transform/opacity also competes with spring-driven inline values.
a11y: No role (dialog/region), no aria-labelledby/aria-describedby, no focus management, no aria-live announcement - a consent banner invisible to screen-reader users until they stumble on it. Uses GlassButton (good). Privacy link opens new tab without warning.
api: forwardRef + rest spread. Spreads unknown props (theme, intent, elevation, tier, motionSensitivity from shared GlobalCookieConsentProps type) onto the DOM div via ...rest -> React unknown-prop warnings. Props type is aliased from GlobalCookieConsentProps, so it advertises onSave/cookieCategories/customContent that it ignores. GlassCookieConsent variant (274-279) is not root-exported and differs only by glassIntensity.
ssr: 'use client'; document.cookie only in effects. Returns a hidden node on SSR then shows after delay - fine.
fake_complexity: CRITICAL BUG: Accept/Decline buttons only call onAccept/onDecline (237, 258); they never set the consent cookie or hide the banner. setCookie and cookieExpiration are defined/accepted but unused (26-31, 86). There is no open/onOpenChange prop, so a consumer cannot dismiss it either - the banner is undismissable except via timeout. Mobile CSS sets transform:none for centered positions but the inline spring transform re-adds translateX(-50%) (184-187 vs module.css:61-74), shifting top/bottom-centered banners half off-screen on <540px; the certification story uses position bottom-right default so this path is not exercised.
target: GlassCookieConsent (single component: variant='compact'|'banner'|'preferences', controlled open/onOpenChange, shared consent store hook)
justification: Its token-based material and wired reduced-motion springs are the most systematic code in this shard. Functionally, though, it is broken: clicking Accept or Decline neither stores consent nor closes the banner, and there's no controlled prop to fix that from outside. It also has no dialog or region semantics and leaks unknown props onto the DOM. All three cookie components copy the same cookie helpers, position map and spring setup. Merge them into one GlassCookieConsent with variants, a useCookieConsent store, proper role and label attributes, and a working dismiss.

stories.notes: Default story forces style position:'static', transform:'none' (103-110), so fixed/centered positioning and the mobile translate bug are never certified.

material_impl: CSS module tokenized surface (GlobalCookieConsent.module.css:12-19); reuses GlassModal, GlassCheckbox, GlassButton, Typography, Box - good primitive reuse.
motion: Galileo springs, reduced-motion respected (116); exit animation never plays (display:none branch 305-315).
a11y: No role/aria-labelledby on banner. Checkbox has no label association - category name is a sibling Typography span (323-332), so each checkbox is unlabeled. 'Show cookie details' button is a no-op with aria-expanded bound to global expanded and aria-controls='cookie-details' (341-351); id 'cookie-details' is static so multiple instances or the modal duplicate it. Modal header close '×' button has no aria-label (452-458).
api: forwardRef + rest spread; theme/intent/elevation/tier/animationConfig/disableAnimation/motionSensitivity leak to DOM. `(expanded || initiallyExpanded)` (405) means initiallyExpanded can never be collapsed. CookieCategory.defaultEnabled is never read. createThemeContext imported unused. No hook to read consent state back (consumers must parse 'cookie-categories' cookie themselves).
fake_complexity: Mostly real (accept/decline/save write cookies), but cookie details expansion is unimplemented (346-353 comments 'could be expanded here'). Cookie values written raw JSON without encodeURIComponent, no SameSite/Secure. Mobile centered-position translate bug shared with CookieConsent (default position is 'bottom').
target: GlassCookieConsent variant='preferences' (base of the consolidated component)
justification: This is the most complete of the three and reuses real primitives (GlassModal, GlassCheckbox, GlassButton), so it should be the base for the consolidated GlassCookieConsent. Before 5.0 it needs labelled checkboxes, a working details disclosure, dialog/region semantics, the mobile centering fix, cookies encoded with SameSite/Secure, an exit animation, and a consent-state hook. It's a utility pattern, not a showcase piece.
